description: The Mesh node under each Component turns the geometry into finite elements. This category covers the physics-controlled and user-controlled meshing sequences, global and local element size control, the free (tetrahedral, triangular, quadrilateral) and structured (mapped, swept) meshers, boundary layers, and the operations that refine, convert, copy, import and adapt an existing mesh. Every node corresponds to a model.component("comp1").mesh("mesh1").create(tag, type) call in the COMSOL API for Java.

tools.name: Physics-Controlled Mesh
tools.description: The default state of every Mesh node: COMSOL inspects the active physics interfaces and builds a meshing sequence suited to the equations, for example adding boundary layers on no-slip walls for fluid flow or resolving skin depth for electromagnetics. You only choose an overall element size on the Extremely coarse to Extremely fine slider. Switch to User-controlled mesh as soon as you need to place a specific mesher on a specific selection; that gives you an editable sequence seeded with the current settings.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > Settings > Mesh > Sequence type: Physics-controlled mesh | User-controlled mesh

parameters.name: Sequence type
parameters.description: Physics-controlled mesh or User-controlled mesh. API: automatic(true) / automatic(false); isAutomatic() reports the current state.

parameters.name: Element size
parameters.description: Predefined size preset. API: autoMeshSize(n) where n = 1 Extremely fine, 2 Extra fine, 3 Finer, 4 Fine, 5 Normal (default), 6 Coarse, 7 Coarser, 8 Extra coarse, 9 Extremely coarse.

tools.notes: Adding or editing any feature switches the sequence to user-controlled automatically. A physics-controlled sequence is regenerated whenever the active physics changes, so a script must never assume a particular feature tag exists in it. Physics-controlled meshing uses built-in heuristics, not numerical error estimates; error-driven refinement comes from the Adapt operation or from Adaptive Mesh Refinement in the study step.

tools.name: Size
tools.description: Sets the element size parameters used by the meshers that follow it in the sequence. With Predefined sizes you pick one of the nine presets; with Custom you set maximum and minimum element size, growth rate, curvature factor and narrow-region resolution directly. A Size node placed at sequence level applies globally, while a Size added inside an Edge, Free Quad, Free Triangular, Free Tetrahedral, Mapped or Swept node (or on a selection) gives local refinement on just those entities.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > Size (default node), or Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Attributes > Size for an extra local size; also right-click a mesher node (e.g. Free Tetrahedral 1) > Size

parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: on | off. off uses the predefined preset in hauto; on activates hmax, hmin, hgrad, hcurve and hnarrow.

parameters.name: hauto
parameters.description: Predefined element size 1-9, where 1 is Extremely fine and 9 is Extremely coarse (default 5, Normal). Used when custom is off.

parameters.name: hmax
parameters.description: Maximum element size. The single most effective knob; default is geometry dependent.

parameters.name: hmin
parameters.description: Minimum element size; stops the mesher generating needle-thin elements in tiny features.

parameters.name: hgrad
parameters.description: Maximum element growth rate between neighbouring elements (default 1.3 or 1.5). Lower values give smoother size transitions and more elements.

parameters.name: hcurve
parameters.description: Curvature factor (default 0.3 or 0.6): element size divided by the local radius of curvature. Smaller resolves curved boundaries better.

parameters.name: hnarrow
parameters.description: Resolution of narrow regions (default 0.5). Larger values force more elements across thin gaps and slivers.

parameters.name: hmaxactive / hminactive / hgradactive / hcurveactive / hnarrowactive
parameters.description: on | off switches that enable each individual custom parameter.

tools.notes: The default Size node has the fixed tag "size" and cannot take a selection; create extra Size attributes (create("size1", "Size")) for local control. The Mapped mesher reads only hauto and hmax from a Size attribute. Sizes are expressions, so "L/20" with a global parameter L keeps the mesh consistent across a parametric sweep.

tools.name: Size Expression
tools.description: Drives the element size from an arbitrary expression instead of a constant, so the mesh can follow a field, a coordinate function or a previously computed solution. The expression is evaluated on a background grid and converted into a size field that the downstream meshers obey. Use it when you know analytically where resolution is needed (near a crack tip, along a beam path, in a boundary layer) or when you want a one-shot solution-driven refinement without a full adaptive loop.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Attributes > Size Expression (also available inside Edge, Free Quad, Free Triangular and Free Tetrahedral nodes)

parameters.name: sizeexpr
parameters.description: Size expression evaluated for the mesh element size; defaults to the geometry bounding-box size.

parameters.name: exprtype
parameters.description: size | error. size interprets the expression as an absolute element size, error as an error indicator to equidistribute.

parameters.name: errorexpr
parameters.description: Error expression used when exprtype is error.

parameters.name: evaltype
parameters.description: grid | solution | initialexpression. Which mesh/state the expression is evaluated on.

parameters.name: gridtype / cellsize / numcell
parameters.description: cellresolution or cellsize background grid; cellsize sets the cell size (default bounding box / 25) and numcell the cells per dimension (default 25).

parameters.name: hmeshgrad
parameters.description: Maximum size-field growth rate, default 1.4 (the size field may grow 40% per element).

parameters.name: elselect
parameters.description: globalmin | worst | elements. How elements are picked for refinement, tuned by globalminparam or elementspar.

tools.notes: Call feature("se1").importData() to re-evaluate the expression after the model changes (for example after a new solution). A coarse background grid can miss thin features - reduce cellsize or raise numcell if the size field looks blocky. For a true error-driven loop use the Adapt operation or Adaptive Mesh Refinement in the study step instead.

tools.name: Free Tetrahedral
tools.description: The general-purpose 3D mesher: fills selected domains with unstructured tetrahedra using a Delaunay algorithm. It handles arbitrary CAD shapes and is the default choice whenever a domain cannot be swept or mapped. Tetrahedra are the most expensive element per unit volume, so reserve them for genuinely three-dimensional regions and sweep the thin, extruded or layered parts instead.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > Free Tetrahedral (then Free Tetrahedral 1 > right-click > Size / Distribution / Corner Refinement for local control)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains to mesh; an empty selection means the remaining (not yet meshed) domains.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: auto | del | dellegacy52. Delaunay meshing algorithm.

parameters.name: optlevel
parameters.description: basic | medium | high. Element-quality optimisation level; higher costs meshing time but removes slivers.

parameters.name: optcurved
parameters.description: on | off (default on). Avoid inverted curved elements on curved boundaries with higher-order geometry shape order.

parameters.name: optlarge / optsmall
parameters.description: on | off. Avoid elements that are too large or too small relative to the size field.

parameters.name: smoothcontrol / smoothmaxiter / smoothmaxdepth
parameters.description: Smoothing across removed control entities, number of smoothing iterations (default 4) and maximum smoothing depth (default 4).

tools.notes: Mesh a domain only once: a Free Tetrahedral placed after a Swept or Boundary Layers node picks up the remaining domains and conforms to the faces already meshed. Memory scales roughly with the element count, so halving hmax in 3D multiplies both element count and solve time by about eight. optlevel high is worth it before a structural or CFD run where sliver elements ruin conditioning.

tools.name: Free Triangular
tools.description: Creates an unstructured triangular mesh in 2D domains or on 3D faces, and can also remesh faces of an imported surface mesh. In 2D it is the standard mesher; in 3D it is used to mesh the source face of a swept mesh, to mesh boundaries before Boundary Layers, or to build a shell/surface mesh. Triangles adapt to any boundary shape but need more elements than quadrilaterals for the same accuracy in smooth regions.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > Free Triangular (in 3D select faces; in 2D select domains)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains in 2D, boundaries in 3D. In 2D an empty selection means the remaining domains; in 3D the default selection is empty.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: auto | af | del. Advancing front (af) usually gives more regular, better-aligned triangles; Delaunay (del) is more robust on difficult boundaries.

parameters.name: narrowreg
parameters.description: on | off. Resolve the mesh with respect to adjacent narrow domain regions.

parameters.name: defectremoval
parameters.description: Relative size factor for identifying local defects; only for 3D meshes that define their own geometric model.

tools.notes: In 3D, a Free Triangular on the source face followed by a Swept operation is the standard recipe for prism meshes in extruded geometries. Add a Distribution on the bounding edges first if you need a specific element count around the face.

tools.name: Free Quad
tools.description: Creates an unstructured quadrilateral mesh in 2D domains or on 3D faces, without requiring the four-sided topology that the Mapped mesher needs. Quads give fewer elements and fewer degrees of freedom than triangles for the same resolution and behave better for flow along a surface, at the cost of some element distortion where the shape is irregular. Use it as the source-face mesher when you want a hexahedral swept mesh in 3D.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > Free Quad (in 3D select faces; in 2D select domains)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains in 2D, boundaries in 3D; the default selection is empty in 3D.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: auto | legacy52 | legacy52a | legacy54. Quad meshing algorithm; auto for new models, legacy values appear in migrated models.

parameters.name: simplifymesh
parameters.description: on | off. Simplify the original mesh; only for imported meshes in 3D.

parameters.name: defectremoval
parameters.description: Relative size factor for local defect identification; only for imported meshes in 3D.

tools.notes: Free Quad on the source face plus Sweep gives hexahedra; Free Triangular plus Sweep gives prisms. If a downstream physics or operation needs simplex elements, add a Convert node after the quad mesher.

tools.name: Mapped
tools.description: Creates a structured quadrilateral mesh by mapping a regular grid on a logical unit square onto each selected 2D domain or 3D face, using transfinite interpolation. It produces the cleanest, cheapest elements available and is ideal for rectangles, annuli and other four-sided regions, and for surfaces that will be swept. It requires the domain to be topologically four-sided (or made so with Edge Groups), otherwise it fails and you must fall back to Free Quad or Free Triangular.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > Mapped (then Mapped 1 > right-click > Distribution / Edge Groups / Size)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains in 2D, boundaries in 3D. In 2D an empty selection means the remaining domains; in 3D the default is empty.

parameters.name: interpmethod
parameters.description: auto | transfinite2D | transfinite3D. Interpolation method for 3D mapped meshes on geometry-conforming sequences.

parameters.name: adjustedgdistr
parameters.description: on | off. Let the mapped mesher adjust an evenly distributed edge mesh.

parameters.name: smoothcontrol / smoothmaxiter / smoothmaxdepth
parameters.description: Mesh smoothing across removed control entities; iterations and depth both default to 4.

parameters.name: Attribute subnodes
parameters.description: Distribution (element count per edge), EdgeGroup (group edges so a many-sided face becomes logically four-sided), Size (uses only hauto and hmax) and Scale.

tools.notes: Opposite edges must carry the same number of elements; conflicting Distribution nodes are the usual cause of a failed mapped mesh. Use Edge Groups to tell COMSOL which edges form each logical side of a face with more than four boundary curves.

tools.name: Swept
tools.description: Builds a 3D mesh by sweeping the face mesh of a source face along a domain to a destination face, producing prisms (from a triangular source) or hexahedra (from a quad source). It is the most efficient way to mesh extruded, revolved or otherwise layered geometry - thin plates, pipes, PCB layers, air gaps - because one element can span the thickness while staying well shaped. Add a Distribution subnode to set the number of element layers through the sweep direction.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > Swept (then Swept 1 > right-click > Distribution or Size)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: 3D domains to sweep; an empty selection means the remaining domains.

parameters.name: sourceface / targetface
parameters.description: Source and destination face selections; left automatic COMSOL detects them from the domain topology.

parameters.name: sweeppath
parameters.description: auto | straight | circular | general. How the sweep path is computed.

parameters.name: facemethod
parameters.description: auto | tri | quad (plus legacy options). Method used to mesh the source face when it has no mesh yet.

parameters.name: Distribution (subnode)
parameters.description: Number of element layers along the sweep; set type/numelem or an explicit distribution to grade the layers.

parameters.name: remeshsourceface
parameters.description: on | off. Whether source faces are remeshed for meshes that define their own geometric model.

tools.notes: A domain can only be swept if source and destination faces are topologically compatible and the side faces are sweepable; split the geometry first if a sweep fails. Sweeping the thin domains and leaving Free Tetrahedral for the rest typically cuts the element count by an order of magnitude in plate, shell and gap models.

tools.name: Distribution
tools.description: An attribute that prescribes how many elements go along an edge (3D), a boundary (2D) or the sweep direction of a domain, and how they are spaced. It is the main tool for grading a mesh: fine near a wall or a crack, coarse in the far field, with an exact element count you control. Add it under Edge, Free Quad, Free Triangular, Free Tetrahedral, Mapped or Swept, or at sequence level with its own selection.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Attributes > Distribution, or right-click a mesher node (Mapped 1, Swept 1, Edge 1) > Distribution

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: number | explicit | predefined. Fixed element count, an explicit list of relative node positions, or a predefined graded distribution. It updates automatically when you set a property from one of the groups.

parameters.name: numelem
parameters.description: Number of elements when type is number (default 5).

parameters.name: equidistant
parameters.description: on | off. Force an equidistant mesh along edges in 3D and boundaries in 2D instead of letting the algorithm adapt to the surroundings.

parameters.name: explicit
parameters.description: double[] of relative vertex placements along the edge when type is explicit (default {0, 1}).

parameters.name: reverse
parameters.description: on | off. Reverse the direction in which the distribution is applied.

tools.notes: For a Mapped mesh opposite edges must end up with the same element count, so contradictory Distribution nodes are the usual cause of a failed structured mesh. The explicit form takes relative coordinates between 0 and 1, which is the easiest way to reproduce a hand-designed grading.

tools.name: Boundary Layers
tools.description: Inserts thin, anisotropic element layers next to selected walls so that steep normal gradients are resolved without refining the whole domain. It is essential for CFD (wall functions, y+ resolution), for heat transfer with convection and for electromagnetic skin-depth problems. The operation itself (BndLayer) holds corner handling, and one or more Boundary Layer Properties subnodes (BndLayerProp) hold the selection and the layer distribution.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > Boundary Layers, then Boundary Layers 1 > Boundary Layer Properties (select the walls there)

parameters.name: blnlayers
parameters.description: Number of boundary layers (BndLayerProp, default 8).

parameters.name: blstretch
parameters.description: Boundary layer stretching factor (default 1.2); layer m has thickness blstretch^(m-1) * blhmin.

parameters.name: inittype
parameters.description: blhminfact | blhmin | blhtot. Whether the first-layer thickness comes from a factor on the default, an absolute first-layer thickness, or a total boundary-layer thickness.

parameters.name: blhminfact / blhmin / blhtot
parameters.description: Thickness adjustment factor (default 1), absolute thickness of the first layer, or total thickness of the boundary layer mesh.

parameters.name: sharpcorners
parameters.description: none | split | trim (default split). How sharp corners in 2D and sharp edges in 3D are handled.

parameters.name: smoothtransition
parameters.description: on | off (default on). Smooth the transition from the layers to the interior mesh.

parameters.name: splitangle / trimmaxangle / layerdec
parameters.description: Corner split angle (default 240 deg), maximum trimming angle in narrow corners (default 50 deg) and the maximum difference in layer count between neighbouring points (default 2).

tools.notes: Boundary Layers must come after the mesher that fills the domain: for an imported mesh the domains must already contain elements, so run Free Tetrahedral first. Layers are automatically thinned or dropped in narrow regions. Too many layers with a large stretch factor produces high aspect-ratio elements that hurt the condition number of the linear system.

tools.name: Edge
tools.description: Meshes selected edges (curves) with 1D elements. In 1D components it is the meshing operation; in 2D and 3D it is used to seed the boundary of a face before a Free Triangular, Free Quad or Mapped operation, so that the surface mesher inherits an exact node distribution. Combine it with Distribution to fix the number of elements along a specific curve, or with Size for a local element size.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Operations > Edge (then Edge 1 > right-click > Distribution or Size)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Edges to mesh. In 1D an empty selection means the remaining entities; in 2D and 3D the default selection is empty.

parameters.name: smoothcontrol
parameters.description: on | off (default on). Smooth the mesh across removed control entities.

parameters.name: smoothmaxiter / smoothmaxdepth
parameters.description: Number of smoothing iterations and maximum smoothing depth, both default 4.

tools.notes: A related Vertex operation meshes isolated points and is used to force a mesh node exactly at a point load or probe location. Edge operations must come before the face and domain meshers in the sequence for their distributions to be respected.

tools.name: Corner Refinement
tools.description: Decreases the element size near sharp re-entrant corners: vertices in 2D and edges in 3D whose interior angle exceeds a threshold. Singular or near-singular fields concentrate exactly there (stress concentrations, flow separation at a backward-facing step, field enhancement at a metal edge), and the extra elements cost almost nothing because they are confined to the corner. COMSOL detects the corners automatically; you can add or remove individual ones with the corner selection.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Attributes > Corner Refinement, or right-click an Edge, Free Quad, Free Triangular or Free Tetrahedral node > Corner Refinement

parameters.name: minangle
parameters.description: Minimum angle (default 240 deg) for a corner to be treated as sharp and refined.

parameters.name: boundary
parameters.description: Boundary selection the refinement applies to.

parameters.name: corner
parameters.description: Explicit selection of corners to include or exclude from the automatic detection; set via selection("corner").

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: include | exclude. Whether the corner selection restricts the refinement to those corners or removes them from it.

tools.notes: Corner Refinement is an attribute, so it must be created inside an Edge, FreeQuad, FreeTri or FreeTet feature (or at sequence level to affect the whole geometry). A sharp corner is a genuine singularity in linear elasticity and potential flow: refining reduces the discretisation error but the exact solution never converges there, so a fillet in the geometry is often the better fix.

tools.name: Refine
tools.description: Splits the elements of an existing mesh, either everywhere or inside a selection or bounding box. Use it for a quick mesh-convergence study (build once, then refine and re-solve) or to add resolution to an imported mesh that you cannot regenerate. Regular refinement multiplies the element count by four in 2D and eight in 3D per refinement, so check memory before refining a large 3D mesh.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Operations > Refine; the Mesh ribbon tab also exposes Refine Mesh for the whole mesh

parameters.name: rmethod
parameters.description: longest | regular. Longest-edge bisection (local, keeps the element count down) or regular refinement (uniform element splitting).

parameters.name: numrefine
parameters.description: Number of refinements to apply (default 1); also accepts an int[] for per-selection counts.

parameters.name: boxcoord
parameters.description: on | off. Restrict refinement to a bounding box defined by xmin/xmax, ymin/ymax, zmin/zmax.

parameters.name: facerep
parameters.description: curved | linear. Face representation used when placing new mesh vertices for meshes that define their own geometric model.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains to refine; by default the whole geometry.

tools.notes: Refinement works on both generated and imported meshes. For a convergence study it is usually cleaner to sweep hmax (or the hauto preset) as a parameter than to stack Refine nodes, because refinement does not improve the geometry approximation on curved boundaries unless facerep is curved.

tools.name: Convert
tools.description: Converts the nonsimplex elements of a 2D or 3D mesh (quadrilaterals, hexahedra, prisms, pyramids) into simplex elements, that is triangles and tetrahedra. Use it when a downstream operation or physics feature requires simplex elements, when an imported hex mesh has to be merged with a tetrahedral mesh, or when a mapped/swept region must be joined to a free-meshed one. The split method controls how many simplices each element becomes.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Operations > Convert

parameters.name: splitmethod
parameters.description: diagonal | center (default diagonal). diagonal splits each quadrilateral into 2 triangles and each hexahedron into 5 tetrahedra; center splits each quadrilateral into 4 triangles and each hexahedron into 28 tetrahedra.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains or faces to convert; empty converts every quadrilateral, pyramidal, prismatic and hexahedral element in the mesh.

tools.notes: Conversion multiplies the element count (and so the degrees of freedom) substantially, especially with the center method, so convert only the regions that need it. In 3D the conversion also splits the quadrilateral faces on the boundaries of the selected domains.

tools.name: Copy Domain
tools.description: Copies the mesh of one set of domains onto another set using a rigid-body transformation with an optional scale factor. Use it for repeated geometry (an array of fins, coil turns, battery cells) to guarantee identical meshes and to save meshing time, and to make source and destination meshes match exactly where a periodic boundary condition or an identity pair is applied. Companion operations Copy Face and Copy Edge do the same for faces and edges.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Operations > Copy Domain (also Copy Face, Copy Edge)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Source domain selection whose mesh is copied.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Destination domain selection that receives the copied mesh.

parameters.name: copymethod
parameters.description: auto | singlecopy | arraycopy. Whether the destination is treated as one copy or as an array of copies.

parameters.name: Orientation attributes
parameters.description: EdgeMap, OnePointMap or TwoPointMap subnodes pin down how the source mesh is oriented on the destination when the automatic match is ambiguous.

parameters.name: smoothcontrol / smoothmaxiter / smoothmaxdepth
parameters.description: Smoothing across removed control entities after the copy.

tools.notes: Periodic Condition and Identity Pair features converge far better when the two sides carry identical meshes, which is exactly what Copy Face provides. Source and destination must be geometrically congruent up to the rigid-body transform and scale factor, otherwise the operation fails.

tools.name: Import (mesh)
tools.description: Imports a mesh from a file, from another meshing sequence, from a geometry sequence or from a Filter/Partition dataset, into a meshing sequence that defines its own geometric model. It is how you bring in a mesh produced by another tool, a scanned STL surface or a NASTRAN volume mesh, and then continue with COMSOL operations such as Convert, Refine, Delete Entities or Boundary Layers. If the sequence already contains a mesh, the imported mesh is added to it.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > Import (set Source to Mesh from file, then browse for the file)

parameters.name: Supported formats
parameters.description: COMSOL .mphtxt and .mphbin; NASTRAN .nas, .bdf, .dat; sectionwise .txt; STL .stl (text and binary); PLY .ply; 3MF .3mf; VRML. 3MF, PLY, STL and VRML are 3D only; in 2D, NASTRAN meshes must have a constant third coordinate.

parameters.name: importData()
parameters.description: Method that re-reads the file, so an updated mesh can be pulled in without rebuilding the node.

parameters.name: Transform (attribute)
parameters.description: Position, rotate or scale the imported mesh after import.

tools.notes: An imported mesh has no CAD behind it, so the sequence defines its own geometric model: use Create Faces, Detect Faces, Join Entities, Delete Entities or Ball/Box element selections to build the boundary partition you need for physics selections. Imported STL surface meshes usually need Fill Holes or Create Domains before a volume mesher can run.

tools.name: Adapt
tools.description: Produces a new mesh from an existing one and a computed solution, refining (and optionally coarsening) where an error indicator or a size expression says resolution is needed. This is the mesh-level counterpart of Adaptive Mesh Refinement in a study step, and it is the right choice when you want to inspect and reuse the adapted mesh instead of letting the solver adapt internally. Method controls whether the mesh is generally modified, regularly refined or refined by longest-edge bisection.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > More Operations > Adapt (set Type of expression, pick the solution, then Build)

parameters.name: exprtype
parameters.description: size | error | metric. Treat the input as an absolute size field, an error expression to equidistribute, or (2D/3D) an anisotropic metric.

parameters.name: errorexpr / sizeexpr / metric
parameters.description: The error expression, the size expression, or the symmetric 2x2 / 3x3 metric matrix (for example {{"2/h","0"},{"0","1/h"}}) that drives the adaptation.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: modify | regular | longest (default longest). General mesh modification, regular refinement or longest-edge refinement.

parameters.name: maxrefinement / maxcoarsening / allowcoarsening
parameters.description: Maximum refinement (default 5) and coarsening (default 5) factors; coarsening is only possible when method is modify.

parameters.name: elselect
parameters.description: globalmin | worst | elements, tuned by globalminparam or elementspar, selects which elements get refined.

parameters.name: adapsolnum / selection
parameters.description: Which solution(s) of a parametric or eigenvalue study to adapt on (first, last, all or manual indices).

tools.notes: Use feature("ada1").importData() to rebuild the adapted mesh after the model or solution changes. Adapt works on imported meshing sequences too. For a fully automatic loop, enable Adaptive Mesh Refinement in the Stationary or Time Dependent study step instead - that repeats solve-estimate-refine without manual intervention.

tools.name: model.mesh("mesh1").run() / autoMeshSize()
tools.description: The two API calls that actually build a mesh. run() executes the whole meshing sequence (the equivalent of clicking Build All), while run(ftag) builds only up to and including one feature, which is useful for debugging a long sequence. autoMeshSize(n) sets the overall predefined element size of a physics-controlled or default-size mesh on the same 1-9 scale as the GUI slider.
tools.usage: model.component("comp1").mesh("mesh1").run(); - or the shorthand model.mesh("mesh1").run(); GUI equivalent: Component 1 > Mesh 1 > right-click > Build All (Build Selected for one feature)

parameters.name: run()
parameters.description: Builds the complete meshing sequence.

parameters.name: run(<ftag>)
parameters.description: Builds the sequence up to and including the feature with that tag.

parameters.name: autoMeshSize(n)
parameters.description: n = 1 Extremely fine ... 5 Normal (default) ... 9 Extremely coarse. Called with no argument it returns the current setting.

parameters.name: automatic(boolean) / isAutomatic()
parameters.description: Switch between physics-controlled (true) and user-controlled (false) sequences, and query the current state.

parameters.name: mesh().create(<tag>, <geomtag>)
parameters.description: Creates a new meshing sequence bound to a geometry sequence, e.g. model.component("comp1").mesh().create("mesh1", "geom1").

tools.notes: model.study("std1").run() rebuilds the mesh automatically if it is out of date, so an explicit run() is mainly needed when you want to inspect or export the mesh first. Element counts and quality measures are shown in the Mesh node's Statistics window (right-click Mesh 1 > Statistics) and as a Mesh plot with Element Quality as the expression; watch for minimum quality below roughly 0.1, which usually signals slivers that will slow or break the linear solver.
